Nobody in that crowd understood why stealing was wrong. So they were given a reason that would actually work.

Picture the meeting: a room full of people who'd never been told not to take their neighbor's cow. "Because it's wrong" meant nothing to them. "Because you'll be struck down" meant everything.

That's where the commandments came from — karma, repackaged as consequence, aimed at people with no other reason to behave. The fear was the delivery system. The mechanism underneath it was real.

The biggest lie about karma isn't a mystical one. It's the one that tells you it's already decided.

It's believing you're stuck with it — that whatever happened 20 years ago, 50 years ago, ten lifetimes ago, has already written the ending, and there's nothing left to do about it now.

The best time to create good karma was decades ago. The second best time is today. Karma is just cause and effect: what's happening in your life right now, you created it. Take responsibility for it instead of blaming other people, and what's coming back to you starts to change.
